# Luma Dissolve

**Blend › Luma Dissolve** · v1.0.0 · 30 frames at 30 fps (12–90)

Scene A dissolves by its own brightness: its highlights vanish first and its shadows last, showing scene B behind.

[Preview video](https://github.com/GTKottman/remotion-transitions/releases/download/media/luma-dissolve@1.0.0.mp4)

## Where it is used

- Dreamy or filmic scene changes
- Silhouettes and high-contrast shots
- Light-to-dark changes

## Use it

```tsx
import { linearTiming, TransitionSeries } from '@remotion/transitions';
import { toPresentation } from './src/core';
import lumaDissolve from './transitions/02-blend/luma-dissolve/luma-dissolve';

<TransitionSeries.Transition
  presentation={toPresentation(lumaDissolve, { /* params */ })}
  timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 30 })}
/>
```

Use `linearTiming`: the transition applies its own easing.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Range | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `softness` | number | `0.25` | 0.02–1 | Width of the dissolve band in brightness. |
| `darkFirst` | boolean | `false` |  | Dissolve the shadows first instead. |
